item.title: Nepal retoma operações de resgate das vítimas das enchentes, busca ajuda técnica e bilhões de dólares
item.description: O Nepal retomou as operações de busca e resgate neste sábado, após uma breve suspensão devido às condições climáticas, enquanto as autoridades procuravam por quase 3.000 pessoas desaparecidas após uma enchente devastadora que matou centenas de pessoas e assolou uma região na fronteira com o Tibete.
item.dc:creator: Gopal Sharma, Saurabh Sharma, Sahana Bajracharya, Liz Lee
item.content:encoded: O Nepal retomou as operações de busca e resgate neste sábado, após uma breve suspensão devido às condições climáticas, enquanto as autoridades procuravam por quase 3.000 pessoas desaparecidas após uma enchente devastadora que matou centenas de pessoas e assolou uma região na fronteira com o Tibete. O empobrecido país himalaio, com 30 milhões de habitantes, solicitou assistência especializada do exterior, e seu ministro da Fazenda disse à Reuters que também precisaria de cerca de US$4 bilhões a US$5 bilhões para a reconstrução após o desastre. Provocada pelo colapso de uma geleira, uma torrente de rochas, gelo, lama e detritos desceu rapidamente pelos sistemas fluviais das montanhas na quarta-feira, matando pelo menos 669 pessoas no Nepal e sete no Tibete chinês, além de arrasar prédios, pontes e usinas de energia. Quase 3.000 pessoas continuam desaparecidas, incluindo 2.426 no Nepal e 554 no condado de Gyirong, no Tibete, entre elas pelo menos 540 estrangeiros, muitos dos quais peregrinos hindus da Índia. CORPOS EM DECOMPOSIÇÃO E IRRECONHECÍVEIS SERÃO ENTERRADOS As operações de busca e resgate foram temporariamente suspensas devido à chuva e ao nevoeiro, mas retomadas no final da tarde (horário local), informou um policial do distrito de Rasuwa, uma das regiões mais atingidas. “Os helicópteros estão voando e a operação foi retomada após uma melhora nas condições climáticas”, disse ele, sob condição de anonimato, pois não está autorizado a falar com a mídia. As autoridades também haviam suspendido os trabalhos de resgate na sexta-feira, quando um lago, formado na fronteira entre o Nepal e a China após a enchente, começou a transbordar para os rios Lhende Khola e Trishuli, no Nepal. Até sábado, o risco havia diminuído e partes do leito do lago estavam visíveis, informaram as autoridades chinesas e a emissora estatal CCTV. Imagens de satélite sugeriram que a água estava escoando lentamente do lago, reduzindo gradualmente seu tamanho, informou a CCTV. O lago é um dos dois a montante da zona de enchentes que estão sendo monitorados pelo Nepal. Os riscos de enchentes persistirão até que ambos tenham esvaziado completamente, alertou uma autoridade. Três dias após o desastre, as autoridades informaram que alguns corpos recuperados estavam em estado de decomposição avançada, impossibilitando a identificação. Eles serão enterrados após o cumprimento das formalidades legais devido aos riscos à saúde e ao temor de surtos de doenças. “Amostras de DNA serão coletadas, e os corpos serão enterrados em um espaço aberto”, informou a administração do distrito de Chitwan em um comunicado. FAMÍLIAS PROCURAM OS DESAPARECIDOS Em Katmandu, familiares das pessoas desaparecidas se reuniram em frente ao Campus Médico de Maharajgunj, para onde alguns corpos haviam sido levados. Muitos tentaram identificar parentes a partir de fotografias dos corpos exibidas nos portões e muros. Na Malásia, familiares de 91 cidadãos listados como “inacessíveis” no Tibete e no Nepal também aguardavam notícias. Manivannan Rethinam, representante de alguns deles, instou o Ministério das Relações Exteriores a estabelecer um canal de comunicação para atualizações mais rápidas, dizendo que a falta de informações era “profundamente dolorosa” para os familiares que aguardavam notícias. O Ministério das Relações Exteriores da Malásia informou que os esforços de busca e resgate, bem como de verificação, continuavam. Para os sobreviventes, o calvário está longe de terminar, já que eles enfrentam a tarefa de reconstruir suas vidas. Saraswati Ghale, de 43 anos, disse que sua casa foi destruída pela enchente. Ela se lembrou de ter subido a colina às pressas quando a água chegou, sacudindo o chão “como se fosse um terremoto”. “Não tenho mais nada... Estou salva, mas quem sabe como as coisas vão se desenrolar”, disse ela. O ministro das Finanças do Nepal, Swarnim Wagle, disse à Reuters que a estimativa inicial do governo era de que a reconstrução custaria entre US$ 4 bilhões e US$ 5 bilhões. “Isso é apenas uma estimativa. As perdas e os danos estão sendo avaliados”, disse ele. AJUDA TÉCNICA O ministro das Relações Exteriores do Nepal, Shisir Khanal, disse que o país não precisava de ajuda nas operações de busca e resgate, mas necessitava de assistência especializada para resgatar pessoas presas em túneis, restaurar as linhas de transporte e comunicação onde as pontes foram destruídas, identificar corpos, realizar testes de DNA e armazenar corpos por períodos mais longos. “Já solicitamos esses serviços especializados e assistência técnica em áreas nas quais não temos expertise e conhecimento técnico suficientes”, disse ele à Reuters na noite de sexta-feira. Uma equipe de especialistas indianos em túneis chegou ao Nepal neste sábado, disse ele, enquanto a agência de notícias chinesa Xinhua informou que Pequim havia enviado cinco especialistas em túneis para apoiar os esforços de resgate, com mais quatro prestes a se juntar a eles. A Índia já enviou três voos transportando 60 toneladas de suprimentos de emergência, incluindo cobertores, medicamentos e alimentos. O país também ofereceu equipes de resposta a desastres, pontes pré-fabricadas e equipes técnicas para ajudar a restaurar a conectividade, informou o Ministério das Relações Exteriores. As autoridades chinesas também correm contra o tempo para localizar mais de 500 pessoas que continuam desaparecidas após a enchente. As equipes de resgate chegaram na sexta-feira ao complexo da passagem de fronteira de Gyirong, o local mais atingido, usando cordas para atravessar florestas e penhascos depois que as estradas que levavam ao local foram destruídas. Imagens de vigilância da passagem de fronteira mostraram torrentes de água e detritos engolindo edifícios quando a enchente atingiu a região, enquanto as pessoas tentavam fugir.

item.title: Pogacar abandona por caída la Vuelta a España cuando marchaba líder
item.description: El líder de la Vuelta a España, Tadej Pogacar, abandonó la carrera el sábado tras sufrir una caída durante la octava etapa que le dejó al cinco veces ganador del Tour de Francia con la cara ensangrentada y una lesión en el hombro.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El líder de la Vuelta a España, Tadej Pogacar, abandonó la carrera el sábado tras sufrir una caída durante la octava etapa que le dejó al cinco veces ganador del Tour de Francia con la cara ensangrentada y una lesión en el hombro. El ciclista esloveno, que llevaba el maillot rojo de líder desde que ganó la primera etapa, sufrió una caída en el pelotón cuando quedaban poco más de 30 kilómetros para el final de la etapa entre Pucol y Xeraco. Pogacar, de 27 años, intentó volver a subirse a la bicicleta tras recibir atención médica, pero no pudo reanudar la carrera y acabó caminando hasta una ambulancia. "Lamentablemente, Tadej Pogacar se ha visto obligado a abandonar la Vuelta tras una caída en la octava etapa", publicó su equipo, el UAE Team Emirates-XRG, en la red social X, confirmando el abandono de su corredor. Pogacar, que ganó su quinto Tour el mes pasado y se había adjudicado el Giro de Italia en 2024, aspiraba a su primera victoria general en la Vuelta para convertirse en el noveno ciclista en ganar las tres grandes vueltas europeas. Comenzó la etapa con una ventaja de tres minutos y 50 segundos sobre el segundo clasificado, Enric Mas. Bryan Coquard (Cofidis) ganó la etapa tras otra caída masiva en el último kilómetro. Mads Pedersen terminó segundo, mientras que Jordi Meeus fue tercero. Mas (Movistar) se hizo con el maillot rojo, convirtiéndose en el primer español en liderar la carrera desde Jesús Herrada en 2018. Félix Gall es segundo en la general, a un minuto y 11 segundos del nuevo líder.

item.title: Israeli settlers stage new attack on home in West Bank's Qusra, witnesses say
item.description: Dozens of masked Israeli settler militants attacked homes surrounding the occupied West Bank village of Qusra on Saturday, the first major attack since a siege by settlers in the area earlier this month drew an international outcry.
item.dc:creator: Pesha Magid
item.content:encoded: Dozens of masked Israeli settler militants attacked homes surrounding the occupied West Bank village of Qusra on Saturday, the first major attack since a [USN:L1N44A0G5 TEXT:"siege by settlers"] in the area earlier this month drew an international outcry. The settlers surrounded a Palestinian home, throwing stones while seven Palestinians were trapped inside, according to witnesses who spoke to Reuters. Saddam Oday, one of those trapped, said the Israeli military fired tear gas into the home and detained the residents inside while letting him go. He said the Israeli military had not detained any of the settlers and had allowed them to leave. The owner of the house, Luay Bayruti, said when the military arrived they handcuffed, blindfolded and beat those inside, before later releasing them. The Israeli military said in a statement that troops and border police forces had arrived on the scene to remove "rioters" and protect the residents inside the house. The military did not immediately respond to a request for comment on why they had reportedly fired tear gas at the house and detained and beaten the residents. In his first public statement on Qusra, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said he condemned the violence in Qusra and blamed a "handful of rioters". "I strongly condemn the criminal acts of violence committed in the villages of Qusra and Jalud," said Netanyahu, referring to a separate incident in a neighbouring village. The United States had previously pressured Netanyahu to publicly condemn the militant settlers who had besieged Palestinians in their homes, U.S. and Israeli officials [USN:L6N44B0L9 TEXT:"told"] Reuters around two weeks ago. The Israeli government has previously [USN:L8N3X215E TEXT:"blamed"] a "fringe minority" for settler violence, a characterisation disputed by findings from rights groups. A U.N. inquiry in June [USN:L6N42H0E8 TEXT:"found"] that Israeli authorities are directly involved in settler attacks that have killed, injured and displaced Palestinians in the occupied West Bank. The Israeli mission in Geneva rejected the report's findings. RESIDENT REPORTS NEAR-DAILY ENCROACHMENTS Bayruti said that after calling the Israeli military for help, he and six others were trapped inside the home for more than an hour as settlers threw stones. Bayruti showed a Reuters reporter his bandaged arm, which he said had been injured by a stone during the attack. Oday, a medic, said four of those trapped had suffered injuries due to the tear gas, and two had suffered injuries from the stones thrown by settlers. The attack occurred a few hundred yards away from three homes to which settlers laid siege this month, drawing [USN:L6N44B0NM TEXT:"international condemnation"] and a massive Israeli military deployment that residents say has kept them effectively trapped in their homes. "They spotted the residents working on their house, which is still under construction and they started throwing rocks," said [USN:L8N44E16L TEXT:"Loui Ridi"], a Palestinian-American whose home was one of the three under siege this month. He said he watched Saturday's attack occur from his home. Ridi said he had seen near-daily encroachments of Israeli settlers into the area surrounding his home, despite the heavy Israeli military presence in the area. SETTLER VIOLENCE ON THE RISE Rights groups say the increasing settler presence on the edge of Palestinian villages, like Qusra, is part of a wider effort by settlers to seize more land from Palestinians, further eating into territory where Palestinians aim to establish a state. Violence by Jewish settlers in the occupied West Bank has increased, with some emboldened by the government of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who has overseen a massive settlement expansion in the territory. U.N. bodies and most countries deem the settlements illegal under international law regarding military occupations. Israel rejects this, viewing the area as disputed rather than occupied.

item.title: Ataque russo a depósito de munições na região de Kiev provoca explosão e mata 37 pessoas
item.description: Pelo menos 37 pessoas morreram depois que um ataque com drone russo a um depósito de munições na região de Kiev provocou uma explosão, afirmou o presidente, Volodymyr Zelenskiy, neste sábado, prometendo punir a suposta negligência no segundo incidente desse tipo em dois meses.
item.dc:creator: Dan Peleschuk
item.content:encoded: Pelo menos 37 pessoas morreram depois que um ataque com drone russo a um depósito de munições na região de Kiev provocou uma explosão, afirmou o presidente, Volodymyr Zelenskiy, neste sábado, prometendo punir a suposta negligência no segundo incidente desse tipo em dois meses. O ataque russo mais mortal na região de Kiev neste ano ocorreu enquanto os ataques aéreos de Moscou contra a capital ucraniana e a região ao redor se estendiam pelo terceiro dia consecutivo, matando moradores, danificando casas e perturbando a vida cotidiana. Dezenas também ficaram feridas e centenas foram retiradas da área do ataque na noite de sexta-feira na vila de Myla, disse Zelenskiy, onde infraestruturas próximas, incluindo edifícios residenciais e um centro para idosos e pessoas com deficiência, sofreram “danos significativos”. O ataque provocou incêndios generalizados, segundo autoridades. Entre os mortos estava o chefe de um vilarejo vizinho que correu para ajudar. “Uma situação terrível e uma negligência terrível por parte daqueles que armazenaram explosivos bem ao lado das pessoas”, disse Zelenskiy em um discurso em vídeo. SEGUNDA DETONAÇÃO RELACIONADA A ATAQUE EM DOIS MESES O local da explosão da sexta-feira era uma instalação militar que abrigava projéteis de artilharia, minas e drones, entre outras munições, acrescentou ele. O incidente seguiu-se a um caso semelhante na cidade de Vyshneve, na região de Kiev, no mês passado, quando 10 pessoas morreram e centenas de casas foram danificadas após um ataque ter provocado explosões secundárias. “Outro crime desse tipo – depois do que aconteceu em Vyshneve – é absolutamente inaceitável”, disse Zelenskiy. “Espero que os detalhes sejam apresentados ao público imediatamente.” Ele acrescentou que já foram abertos processos criminais sob a acusação de negligência oficial. Autoridades ucranianas raramente divulgam os danos causados a alvos militares por ataques russos. Em comunicado divulgado neste sábado, o Ministério da Defesa da Ucrânia afirmou que todos os responsáveis pelo armazenamento de armas devem realizar uma auditoria completa em suas instalações. ENXAMES DE DRONES ASSOLAM KIEV POR DIAS Outras nove regiões foram alvo de ataques noturnos da Rússia, acrescentou Zelenskiy, dizendo que Kiev, em particular, estava sob um “ataque praticamente ininterrupto” de drones a jato. A Rússia intensificou sua guerra aérea contra a Ucrânia com um número crescente de mísseis balísticos difíceis de detectar e novos drones de alta velocidade, contra os quais Kiev não possui defesas aéreas capazes de abatê-los. Neste sábado, sirenes soaram durante toda a manhã e a tarde pelo terceiro dia consecutivo, enquanto a Força Aérea da Ucrânia alertava sobre novas ondas de drones se aproximando da capital. O som das defesas aéreas ressoou pelo céu. O governador da região de Kiev, Tymur Tkachenko, disse que uma menina de 14 anos morreu em um ataque com drones pela manhã no distrito de Boryspil. Em Kiev, uma menina de 2 anos foi morta por um drone abatido, informou o prefeito Vitali Klitschko neste sábado. Os ataques na cidade e nos arredores, na quinta e na sexta-feira, causaram danos a prédios residenciais e instalações de armazenamento pertencentes a grandes varejistas, parte do que algumas autoridades ucranianas descreveram como uma campanha destinada a “paralisar” a cidade de vários milhões de habitantes.

item.title: New boss Iraola encouraged despite Liverpool's winless start
item.description: Andoni Iraola is still waiting for his first Premier League victory as Liverpool boss, but he saw enough in Saturday's 2-2 draw with Nottingham Forest to reinforce his belief that the foundations of his new-look side are beginning to take shape.
item.dc:creator: Lori Ewing
item.content:encoded: Andoni Iraola is still waiting for his first Premier League victory as Liverpool boss, but he saw enough in Saturday's [USN:L8N44Q03D TEXT:"2-2 draw"] with Nottingham Forest to reinforce his belief that the foundations of his new-look side are beginning to take shape. The former Bournemouth manager was hired this summer to revive a team bruised by last season's failed title defence, when Liverpool crashed from champions in 2025 to fifth place despite spending a Premier League record £446 million on new players. His remit is to restore Liverpool to the summit of English football and reintroduce the intensity that once made Anfield one of Europe's most daunting venues. Iraola's answer is not caution. The Spaniard wants his side to play on the front foot, attack at pace and press relentlessly, a style that should resonate with supporters who spent years watching Juergen Klopp's "heavy-metal football" before the more measured approach of Arne Slot's two-year reign. The transition, however, remains a work in progress. Forest's opening goal from Dan Ndoye stemmed from a direct counterattack, while long periods of a sluggish first half left Iraola frustrated. "I think we improved a lot in the second half. We were much more intense, much quicker on the ball, with more sense of urgency," he said. "But it's not enough to win the game, and I think we have to blame the first half that we had." The improvement after the break was unmistakable. Alexander Isak levelled shortly after the hour mark, before newcomer Victor Munoz struck the late equaliser. Six days earlier, the Spaniard had won the crucial late penalty that secured a [USN:L6N44K05N TEXT:"2–2 draw"] with Newcastle in their opener. "I think Victor has been very good both games," Iraola said. "Everything hasn't been perfect, but he's continued trying all the time and he's gone again and again and again. I like this a lot from the wingers. "He has always been a threat, and also defensively has helped us a lot." SLOW STARTERS The bigger concern for Iraola is Liverpool's tendency to start slowly, a habit they have carried over from last season. While he was encouraged by the character shown to recover from a losing position for a second consecutive match, he believes the underlying issue lies in their work without the ball. "In the first half we were being passive without the ball, leaving a lot of distance and becoming a little bit comfortable," he said. "When we improved the intensity, we won more duels and started attacking quicker and attacking better. This lack of intensity without the ball has hurt us." There is little panic around Anfield, despite the winless start. Iraola has said the tactical shift would take time, and his insistence on playing at a higher tempo was never likely to be mastered overnight. Reinforcements are also on the way. Liverpool have finalised an agreement to sign France winger [USN:L4N44Q01S TEXT:"Bradley Barcola"] from Paris St Germain, according to British media reports, with the 23-year-old's pace and direct running seen as an ideal fit for Iraola's high-octane system. For now, Liverpool remain caught between promise and progress. The entertainment value is increasing, but the victories have yet to arrive. "It's true that we've come back from two bad results where we were losing," Iraola said. "But at the end what makes the difference are the wins and three points. "I liked what we've done in the second half, we've been able to complete the comeback, but the point leaves you frustrated."

item.title: Pogacar forced to abandon Vuelta after stage eight crash, Mas takes overall lead
item.description: Tadej Pogacar's bid to complete cycling's Grand Tour hat-trick came to a painful end at the Vuelta a Espana on Saturday when the race leader and five-time Tour de France winner crashed out with blood on his face and an injured shoulder.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Tadej Pogacar's bid to complete cycling's Grand Tour hat-trick came to a painful end at the Vuelta a Espana on Saturday when the race leader and [USN:L1N43S04R TEXT:"five-time Tour de France winner"] crashed out with blood on his face and an injured shoulder. Slovenia's Pogacar, who had been wearing the red jersey since winning the first stage, went down in the peloton with more than 30 km (19 miles) left in the ride from Pucol to Xeraco. A television replay showed the 27-year-old swerving onto his right, colliding with another rider before going down. He was also hit by other riders coming from behind, a couple of whom also fell. He tried to stand up and get back on his bike as his teammates stopped around him, but he sat back down as medics rushed to him. He later walked into an ambulance with his arm in a sling, with the team announcing that he was facing surgery. “Unfortunately, Tadej suffered a heavy crash during today’s stage and was unable to continue the race," Dr. Adrian Rotunno, Medical Director, UAE Team Emirates-XRG said in a statement. "He is stable, and following a thorough medical assessment at hospital, Tadej has been diagnosed with a concussion, displaced left clavicle fracture, a stable C7 cervical fracture, and multiple abrasions. "Fortunately, no other major injuries and no neurological fallout. He will require clavicle surgery which will be delayed due to concussion precautions. Tadej remains under the care of our medical team and we’ll provide further updates following the surgery.” Pogacar, who won his fifth Tour de France last month and also won the Giro d'Italia in 2024, was aiming for his first overall victory in the Vuelta. That would have made him only the ninth rider to have won all three of cycling's Grand Tours. He began the stage with a lead of three minutes and 50 seconds over second-placed Enric Mas. Mas (Movistar) took the red jersey after stage eight, becoming the first Spaniard to lead the Vuelta since Jesus Herrada in 2018. Pogacar's compatriot Primoz Roglic, a four-time winner of the Vuelta, now lies second, a minute behind Mas. SUBDUED PODIUM Frenchman Bryan Coquard (Cofidis) won the stage after several riders fell in another crash in the final kilometre. Mads Pedersen finished second while Jordi Meeus was third. On the podium, a sombre Mas accepted the red jersey but did not wear it, holding it in front of him instead. "It’s a real shame," Mas said about Pogacar's crash. "I hope he gets better quickly. We've still got a few races left and I hope he'll be in good shape for them." Pogacar's teammates who had stopped for him finally crossed the finish line nearly 12 minutes after the peloton. The race continues on Sunday with a 187.5 km mountainous ride from Villajoyosa to Alto de Aitana.

item.title: La cadena pública italiana RAI destituye a periodista veterano, desatando una tormenta política
item.description: Los partidos de la oposición italiana han denunciado un ataque a la libertad de prensa después de que la cadena pública RAI destituyera a un periodista veterano como presentador de su programa estrella de investigación, mientras que los aliados del Gobierno acogieron con satisfacción la medida.
item.dc:creator: Gavin Jones
item.content:encoded: Los partidos de la oposición italiana han denunciado un ataque a la libertad de prensa después de que la cadena pública RAI destituyera a un periodista veterano como presentador de su programa estrella de investigación, mientras que los aliados del Gobierno acogieron con satisfacción la medida. El caso ha reavivado un debate de larga data sobre la independencia de la RAI, cuya junta directiva es nombrada por el Parlamento y el Gobierno y cuya línea editorial, según los críticos, viene determinada por la coalición gobernante de turno. La RAI anunció el viernes por la noche la destitución de Sigfrido Ranucci tras nueve años al frente de "Report", uno de los programas de actualidad más vistos e influyentes de Italia. "Ya no presentaré 'Report', pero lideraré la batalla más importante de mi vida: la lucha por la libertad de prensa", declaró Ranucci tras conocer la decisión. El "caso Ranucci" ha acaparado la atención de los medios italianos durante semanas, y su destitución fue la noticia principal en los principales periódicos italianos el sábado. El caso se inició con un atentado con bomba frente a la vivienda de Ranucci en octubre, que en un primer momento suscitó mensajes de apoyo hacia él procedentes de todo el espectro político. La primera ministra Giorgia Meloni, cuyo partido fue a menudo objeto de investigaciones por parte de "Report", condenó el "grave acto de intimidación" y el Gobierno afirmó que se reforzaría la escolta policial de Ranucci. Sin embargo, la postura de los políticos del Gobierno cambió bruscamente cuando el empresario Valter Lavitola, colaborador de Ranucci desde hacía mucho tiempo, fue detenido este mes y, según su abogado, declaró a la fiscalía que él había ordenado el atentado. Las autoridades hallaron pruebas de que Ranucci tuviera conocimiento previo del atentado, pero la detención de Lavitola desencadenó una avalancha de artículos en los medios progubernamentales en los que se alegaba la existencia de un complot para impulsar la popularidad de Ranucci de cara a una posible incursión en la política. La reacción política a su destitución refleja profundas divisiones en torno a la RAI, cuya gestión, según llevan tiempo afirmando los críticos, es vulnerable a la influencia del Gobierno. "Report" es uno de los pocos programas de investigación de la televisión italiana, donde el panorama de la radiodifusión privada está históricamente vinculado a la política de centroderecha. Elly Schlein, líder del Partido Demócrata de centroizquierda, fue una de las varias figuras de la oposición que afirmaron que la destitución de Ranucci demostraba que debilitar "Report" había sido un objetivo de larga data del Gobierno de derechas de cara a las elecciones previstas para el próximo año. Los aliados de Meloni adoptaron una postura diferente. El viceprimer ministro Matteo Salvini, líder del partido nacionalista La Liga, elogió la decisión, afirmando que era la "correcta" y pidiendo que se aclaren las cuestiones relacionadas con Ranucci. El presidente del Senado, Ignazio La Russa, del partido Hermanos de Italia de Meloni, también expresó su satisfacción, tras haber criticado con frecuencia la línea editorial del programa. La RAI no hizo referencia a las recientes polémicas, limitándose a afirmar que quería reforzar su periodismo de investigación y promover el talento joven. Ofreció a Ranucci un puesto en otros programas de información o como corresponsal en el extranjero. Sin embargo, para aumentar la presión sobre la cadena pública, los periodistas que trabajan en "Report" emitieron un comunicado en el que calificaban la decisión de "inaceptable" y advertían de que muchos miembros de la redacción abandonarían el programa si la dirección no daba marcha atrás.

item.title: Kremlin diz que vê União Europeia como hostil e não há perspectiva de melhora nas relações
item.description: A Europa está fazendo declarações que sugerem que considera a Rússia um “adversário e até mesmo um inimigo”, afirmou o porta-voz do Kremlin, Dmitry Peskov, neste sábado, acrescentando que Moscou não vê perspectivas de melhora nas relações entre a Rússia e a União Europeia.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A Europa está fazendo declarações que sugerem que considera a Rússia um “adversário e até mesmo um inimigo”, afirmou o porta-voz do Kremlin, Dmitry Peskov, neste sábado, acrescentando que Moscou não vê perspectivas de melhora nas relações entre a Rússia e a União Europeia. Não ficou claro imediatamente a quais declarações Peskov se referia. Ele acrescentou que os atuais políticos da UE adotam uma postura de confronto em relação à Rússia, “não apenas nas palavras, mas também nos atos”. “Eles estão mobilizando os recursos militares da Europa e direcionando-os contra nosso país, ao mesmo tempo em que participam diretamente das hostilidades contra nós”, disse Peskov.

item.title: Brevis leads South Africa to victory over Zimbabwe in T20 Tri-Series
item.description: Dewald Brevis smashed an unbeaten 75 from 32 balls as South Africa defeated Zimbabwe by seven wickets in the second match of the Tri-Series also involving hosts Namibia in Windhoek on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Dewald Brevis smashed an unbeaten 75 from 32 balls as South Africa defeated Zimbabwe by seven wickets in the second match of the Tri-Series also involving hosts Namibia in Windhoek on Saturday. South Africa have a depleted squad for the series, having rested most of their regulars, but bounced back from defeat to Namibia on Friday to chase down their victory target with 38 balls remaining. Zimbabwe posted 144 for eight in their 20 overs, but South Africa replied with ease as they posted 146 for three. Zimbabwe made a fast start to their innings, with an opening stand of 45 in 5.1 overs between Brian Bennett (34 from 35 balls) and Ben Curran (24 from 12 balls). As they did against Namibia on Friday, South Africa’s spinners managed to peg them back though, with Prenelan Subrayen (2-27 in 4 overs) and Bjorn Fortuin (1-25 in 4 overs) bowling with control through the middle of the innings. Lanky fast bowler Duan Jansen, twin brother of South Africa all-rounder Marco Jansen, was expensive in his second international, but returned figures of 3-45 in his 4 overs. Namibia host Zimbabwe in the third match in the Tri-Series at the same venue on Monday.

item.title: Franco Fontana, Italian master of colour photography, dies at 92
item.description: Franco Fontana, an Italian photographer famous for turning landscapes into abstract images through the masterful use of colour, geometry and shadows, has died at the age of 92, Italian media reported on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Alvise Armellini
item.content:encoded: Franco Fontana, an Italian photographer famous for turning landscapes into abstract images through the masterful use of colour, geometry and shadows, has died at the age of 92, Italian media reported on Saturday. Starting his career in the 1960s, when black and white still dominated fine art photography, Fontana was a pioneer of colour, influenced by abstract expressionism and minimalism. Some of his best-known pictures — showing southern Italian beaches or countryside in stark, bright colours, sometimes featuring a single tree, cloud or human shadow — evoked the work of abstract painter Mark Rothko. "I believe that (photography) should not document reality, but interpret it," he said in a statement for his 2014 "Full Color" exhibition. "Reality is a bit like a block of marble. You can use it to make an ashtray, or Michelangelo's 'Pieta'," he added, referring to the sculpture in St Peter's Basilica. Fontana was also celebrated for his urban landscapes, both in Italy and the United States, which typically played with stark lines, shadows, and details of parked cars, and for his nude photography. Born in Modena, northern Italy, on December 9, 1933, Fontana never left his hometown, turning down an offer to move to New York while working for Vogue America. A school dropout, he developed an interest in photography during military service and started experimenting with it, first as an amateur, in the early 1960s. In the following decades, he had more than 400 personal exhibitions, worked in fashion and advertising, and had his work displayed in more than 50 museums around the world. In Rome, he was celebrated with a major retrospective, featuring more than 200 photographs, that ran from December 2024 to August 2025.

item.title: Angels' resiliency to be put to test in rematch vs. Phillies
item.description: Despite seeing his team lose an American League-high 83 games, Los Angeles Angels manager Kurt Suzuki has gone out of his way to praise his club's resiliency.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Despite seeing his team lose an American League-high 83 games, Los Angeles Angels manager Kurt Suzuki has gone out of his way to praise his club's resiliency. "They never give up," Suzuki said after the Angels lost their fifth straight game in true gut-punch fashion. Los Angeles dropped a 5-3 decision to the Philadelphia Phillies on Friday night in the opener of a three-game series in Anaheim, Calif. Pinch-hitter Edmundo Sosa hit a grand slam with two outs in the top of the ninth to help rally the Phillies to victory. Sosa's first career grand slam came one batter after Los Angeles outfielder Wade Meckler made a highlight-reel catch to rob Bryson Stott of a go-ahead three-run homer. Angels closer Ben Joyce walked J.T. Realmuto to load the bases before giving way to Sammy Peralta. Sosa deposited a 1-1 changeup over the fence in left-center field for Philadelphia's first go-ahead grand slam with two outs in the ninth inning of a game since Shane Victorino in 2009. Los Angeles also surrendered a late lead in a 4-3 setback to the Cleveland Guardians on Wednesday. "It's part of the game," Meckler told the Orange County Register after Friday night's latest meltdown. "Baseball is tough. Everybody is good and it's part of the game." The Angels will put Suzuki's resiliency theory to the test on Saturday when they try to rebound against Philadelphia left-hander Cristopher Sanchez. Sanchez (16-4, 2.62 ERA), one of the candidates for the National League Cy Young Award, is tied for the major league lead in victories. He hasn't lost a game since July 6 at Kansas City. Sanchez, who is 0-0 with a 5.73 ERA in three career appearances (two starts) against Los Angeles, also is closing in on a couple of impressive milestones. He needs six more strikeouts to reach 200 for the second straight season, and he needs four more wins to become the Phillies' first 20-game winner since Hall of Famer Roy Halladay in 2010. "It would be an honor to be in a position to get to 20 wins," Sanchez recently told MLB.com. "But my first goal is always to throw as many quality innings as I can for the team and always leave the team in good position to win games whenever I'm out there on the mound." Friday's comeback win moved Philadelphia three games ahead of the San Diego Padres for the second NL wild-card spot and 3 1/2 games in front of Arizona for the final wild-card spot. Rookie right-hander Ryan Johnson (3-7, 5.75) will make his first career start against Philadelphia. Johnson carried a no-hit bid into the sixth inning in his most recent start at Texas last Saturday before allowing a leadoff single to Cody Freeman. He left after throwing a career-high seven innings, allowing just the one hit and no runs in a 3-0 victory. "He's been trending up," Suzuki said of Johnson. "Stuff's getting better. He's getting more consistent. He believes in himself. ... When you throw with confidence, you tend to keep getting better and better." Johnson has a 1.69 ERA in his last four starts. --Field Level Media

item.title: Unrelenting Djokovic refuses to give up on record major dream as US Open begins
item.description: The 146th edition of the U.S. Open kicks off on Sunday, with former finalist and local favorite Jessica Pegula launching her bid to win her maiden Grand Slam, while Novak Djokovic continues his quest for a record 25th major.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The 146th edition of the U.S. Open kicks off on Sunday, with former finalist and local favorite Jessica Pegula launching her bid to win her maiden Grand Slam, while Novak Djokovic continues his quest for a record 25th major. Two-time winner Venus Williams will make her 26th appearance in the main draw, while Marta Kostyuk, who reached the semi-finals in the last two majors, looks to carry that momentum into the last Grand Slam of the year. TOP MEN'S MATCH: NOVAK DJOKOVIC V MARIANO NAVONE Since winning the U.S. Open in 2023, Djokovic has reached two Grand Slam finals and six semi-finals, but a 25th major trophy, which would take him past Margaret Court to become the single most successful player in tennis history, has remained just beyond his reach. But the 39-year-old, ranked fifth in the world, remains defiant in his pursuit, shrugging off the idea of retiring any time soon in a documentary about his life released earlier this month. “I know a lot of people are retiring me already, for many years,” he said in the documentary "Novak Djokovic: the Wolf in Winter". “Why would you want me to retire when I am still playing and competing at the highest level? I’m still top-five, top-10 in the world. Why would I talk about retirement when I am proving to myself that I can still win?” Last year, Djokovic lost in the semi-finals of all four Grand Slams. He reached the Australian Open final this year, before reaching the last four at Wimbledon. "I guess for 99% of the players, that would be a very good Grand Slam result. For me, it's good but not good enough, because I'm blessed and cursed to be used to something of a highest degree in terms of results and achievements," Djokovic said after his Wimbledon loss in July. TOP WOMEN'S MATCH: JESSICA PEGULA V ELENA-GABRIELA RUSE The closest Pegula has got to a Grand Slam title was on home soil, where she went down fighting to Aryna Sabalenka in the 2024 U.S. Open final. Last year, Sabalenka knocked her out again, this time in the semis. “I always feel like I'm close. I always feel I can go out, and I can beat these girls," Pegula said after last year's U.S. Open exit. "Even though maybe I don't have the massive weapon that some of them have, or the flashiness that some of them have, I feel like I'm always right there every time I play them." This year, Pegula has reached the semi-finals of the Australian Open, and the quarters at Wimbledon. She also reached the finals of the Washington Open and Cincinnati Open in the lead-up to the U.S. Open. But the 32-year-old is not keen to dwell on defeats. "You just kind of have to wipe it and move on and move forward and keep working on some stuff that I want to get better," she said ahead of her 10th main draw appearance at Flushing Meadows. KOSTYUK LOOKS TO BUILD ON STRONG SEASON Kostyuk made her Grand Slam main draw debut in 2018, but it took her a few years to establish herself on the circuit. She had turned heads with a run to the Australian Open quarter-finals in 2024, but the 24-year-old has finally hit her stride this year, reaching the semis of the French Open and Wimbledon. She holds a career-best ranking of 11th in the world going into the U.S. Open, and has the opportunity to scale greater heights as she kicks off her campaign at the Grandstand against Australia's Storm Hunter. “I want to cherish this moment. I want to appreciate how far we've all come, me and my team,” Ukraine's Kostyuk said after her Wimbledon exit following a loss to champion Linda Noskova last month. "You don’t know how your life is going to look tomorrow, today, whenever. Hopefully, I will get more opportunities, but you never know if you will." item.title: La guerra lastra la economía de Irán mientras EEUU intensifica las sanciones
item.description: Los dirigentes iraníes están reconociendo el impacto económico de la guerra con Estados Unidos, con el líder supremo instando al Gobierno a hacer frente a las dificultades y el presidente afirmando que el comercio exterior se redujo en un tercio debido a las sanciones y al bloqueo estadounidenses.
item.dc:creator: Eman Abouhassira, Yasmine Ghania, Ahmed Tolba
item.content:encoded: Los dirigentes iraníes están reconociendo el impacto económico de la guerra con Estados Unidos, con el líder supremo instando al Gobierno a hacer frente a las dificultades y el presidente afirmando que el comercio exterior se redujo en un tercio debido a las sanciones y al bloqueo estadounidenses. Sin embargo, Teherán no dio señales de retroceso el sábado, y se comprometió a resistir la presión, seguir por la vía diplomática y mantener lo que, según afirma, es su control sobre el estrecho de Ormuz, la vía navegable estratégica que otorga a Irán influencia gracias a su capacidad para perturbar los mercados energéticos mundiales. El Gobierno dijo en un comunicado difundido por los medios estatales que hacer frente a las presiones económicas provocadas por las sanciones y la guerra es una prioridad fundamental, lo que incluye frenar la inflación, gestionar los mercados, crear empleo, orientar la inversión hacia la producción nacional y reducir gradualmente la dependencia del dólar. Seis meses después de que Estados Unidos e Israel iniciaran la guerra, las negociaciones se encuentran en un punto muerto y la Administración del presidente Donald Trump ha intensificado sus esfuerzos para castigar financieramente a Irán con lo que ha calificado como un "Día D económico". SANCIONES AGRAVAN IMPACTO Washington ha advertido a los países de que deben romper sus lazos comerciales con Teherán o se enfrentarán a sanciones secundarias, aunque el Departamento del Tesoro no ha penalizado aún a los principales socios comerciales de Irán, como China e India, lo que podría tener repercusiones para la economía estadounidense y mundial. El Tesoro impuso sanciones al banco egipcio Banque Misr por mantener relaciones comerciales con Teherán, proponiendo una norma que impediría a las sucursales del banco en Emiratos Árabes Unidos realizar transacciones en dólares. El Banco Central de Egipto afirmó que, junto al Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores, están en contacto con funcionarios estadounidenses en relación con este asunto, y añadió que la medida se limita a las transacciones en dólares de Banque Misr en EAU con bancos corresponsales. Banque Misr declaró más tarde en un comunicado que estaba analizando la notificación del Tesoro y añadió que su sucursal en EAU sigue prestando servicios bancarios a sus clientes de conformidad con las normas y procedimientos aplicables. Estados Unidos también impuso sanciones contra una entidad con sede en Hong Kong y una persona vinculada al Banco Melli de Irán, según un aviso publicado en la página web del Tesoro. Esta oleada de sanciones agrava el impacto de la guerra en la economía iraní, donde la inflación anual alcanzó el 66% el mes pasado. El líder supremo, el ayatolá Mojtaba Jamenei —que no ha sido visto en público desde que resultó herido en el ataque inicial del 28 de febrero, en el que murió su padre y antiguo dirigente máximo, el ayatolá Ali Jamenei— instó al Gobierno a hacer frente a las dificultades económicas. "Es necesario abordar con seriedad la cadena de retos económicos y de subsistencia, como la inflación, el desempleo, la gestión de los precios y el mercado de bienes y servicios", señaló una declaración escrita atribuida a Jamenei. El presidente Masoud Pezeshkian declaró a los medios estatales que las exportaciones e importaciones iraníes se habían desplomado casi un 35% debido a las sanciones estadounidenses y al bloqueo naval de los puertos iraníes. No obstante, señaló que Irán pudo vender unos 90 millones de barriles de petróleo durante el efímero memorándum de entendimiento que Estados Unidos e Irán firmaron en junio, cuando Washington permitió las ventas de petróleo iraní. DIPLOMACIA Y DEFENSA Mientras Estados Unidos se centra en su campaña de presión económica, otros han intentado reactivar los esfuerzos diplomáticos para poner fin a la guerra. El primer ministro de Qatar, el jeque Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, se reunió el jueves con líderes iraníes en Teherán. Afirmó que durante la reunión destacó la importancia de volver a la situación prebélica, con un tráfico marítimo sin restricciones a través del estrecho de Ormuz. El ministro de Relaciones Exteriores iraní, Abbas Araqchi, calificó el viernes las conversaciones con Al Thani de "creativas". En un comunicado emitido el sábado, Irán afirmó que la diplomacia y la defensa eran "dos alas complementarias, coordinadas e inseparables" para proteger los intereses nacionales, la seguridad y la integridad territorial del país. Señaló que seguiría ambas vías de manera equilibrada. Qatar —aliado de Estados Unidos y vecino de Irán— y Pakistán ayudaron a mediar en el memorándum de entendimiento de junio que condujo a un breve alto el fuego, antes de que las discrepancias sobre el estrecho lo hicieran fracasar. Antes de la guerra, por esa vía navegable circulaba el 20% del petróleo y del GNL del mundo. Los mandos militares estadounidenses afirman que sus fuerzas han retirado del estrecho las minas marinas que el Cuerpo de la Guardia Revolucionaria Islámica de Irán había colocado hace meses. Trump ha afirmado en repetidas ocasiones que el estrecho de Ormuz está abierto, pero la Marina de la Guardia Revolucionaria declaró en un comunicado que tales afirmaciones "son una mentira evidente", reiterando que la vía marítima sigue cerrada a los buques sin permiso iraní. Solo siete buques de mercancías atravesaron el estrecho el jueves, frente a los 17 del día anterior y por debajo de la media de los últimos 10 días, que es de 15, según datos preliminares de tráfico marítimo publicados el viernes.

item.title: Brewers seek to continue small-ball success vs. Rangers
item.description: The Milwaukee Brewers have earned the best record in Major League Baseball this season by doing the little things.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Milwaukee Brewers have earned the best record in Major League Baseball this season by doing the little things. That's the formula manager Pat Murphy's team will look to employ again Saturday as it hosts the Texas Rangers. While the Brewers rank last in the majors with just 123 home runs, they make up for it by having the MLB's best on-base percentage (.339). That showed in Friday's 6-1 win over the Rangers in the opener of the three-game series. Milwaukee had 14 hits, with two doubles as the only extra-base hits, to go along with four walks. The Brewers' leadoff hitter Brice Turang started the first inning with a bunt single, moving to second on an error, and he would eventually score. They put the game away, scoring twice in the eighth, an inning that started with bunt singles by Sal Frelick and David Hamilton. According to FanGraphs, Milwaukee has bunted during 74 plate appearances this season, the most in the NL. While the Brewers rank third in the majors with 30 sacrifices, Murphy said after Friday's win, it's not always about moving a runner over. Turang, Frelick and Hamilton all hit left-handed, and they got their bunt singles against lefty pitchers. "There's times when we leave our lefties in there," Murphy said. "They're some of our better hitters and can do some things. I don't know how many bunt hits we had today, but we had a few. Sometimes it's easier to bunt left-on-left with that guy falling the other way. We executed that three or four times perfectly." Texas manager Skip Schumaker said he knew what the Brewers' strategy would be before the game. "They've been doing it all year, and that's why their record is what it is. ... If they execute the bunt, it's tough to get them out," he said. While Milwaukee has succeeded with small ball, the Rangers have struggled to score. Their 544 runs scored are the fourth-fewest in the majors. Joc Pederson, the Rangers designated hitter who is tied with first baseman Jake Burger with a team-best 23 home runs, has struggled over the last couple weeks. He has two hits in his last 32 at-bats (.063). The Rangers will look to end their three-game losing streak with veteran Cal Quantrill (6-4, 2.90 ERA) getting the start. The right-hander has won his last two games, including last Sunday when he blanked the Los Angeles Angels over six innings and allowed just six hits and no walks while striking out six in the Rangers' 5-3 home victory. Quantrill has faced Milwaukee four times, including three starts. He has yet to record a decision but has a 3.14 ERA in 14 1/3 innings. His last start against the Brewers took place on July 25, 2025, as a member of the Miami Marlins. In five innings, Quantrill held the Brewers to just three hits and a run with four strikeouts as Miami would pull out a 5-1 victory. Milwaukee will send out rookie Shane Drohan (6-5, 3.84). The lefty has been battered recently, as he has a 5.45 ERA over his last seven starts. However, he allowed the Atlanta Braves just two runs over five innings last Sunday but still came away with the loss as the Braves prevailed 4-2 in the MLB Little League Classic in Williamsport, Pa. -Field Level Media

item.title: Rays ride big day, big inning into rematch vs. Padres
item.description: In terms of a winning the whole day from start to finish, the Tampa Bay Rays will have a hard time topping Friday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: In terms of a winning the whole day from start to finish, the Tampa Bay Rays will have a hard time topping Friday. The Rays, who secured their future in the area early in the day, opened their series against the San Diego Padres with a 9-4 victory. They will try to beat the Padres again on Saturday in St. Petersburg, Fla. Tampa Bay scored five times on just two hits in the fourth inning, building a six-run lead on their way to improving their home record to an American League-best 44-23. Junior Caminero stretched his hitting streak to 11 games with an RBI single. Earlier Friday, Hillsborough County Commissioners voted 5-2 to proceed with funding for the franchise's new $2.3 billion stadium across Tampa's waterway and close to the Buccaneers' football stadium. The project, called the Rays' "Forever Home" by the front office, is expected to be ready for the 2029 season. "Excited for our fans," said manager Kevin Cash, a Tampa native. "A lot of hard work. A lot to be excited about. We experienced Tampa baseball last year playing at Steinbrenner Field. I don't single out Tampa or St. Pete or Sarasota or Bradenton. To me, it's the Tampa Bay area, and I think that's special for our entire fanbase." San Diego starter Casey Mize threw a comebacker into left field later that night that could have started a double play. Instead, the Rays plated five unearned runs. "Things kind of just snowballed from (the throwing error)," Padres manager Craig Stammen said. "Not our prettiest game on any side of the ball tonight." Saturday's matchup will feature two right-handers who are trending up. The Padres will send out Walker Buehler (8-6, 4.63) for his 27th start. The San Diego hurler has earned the victory in two of his past three starts, beating the Minnesota Twins on Sunday and the Milwaukee Brewers on Aug. 11 after allowing one run in six innings in both outings. Sandwiched in between that was a 2-1 loss in New York to the Mets in which he yielded two runs on two hits in yet another six-inning effort. "I think he smells the postseason," Stammen said. "That's one thing that's part of his career is being a part of that every single year. So he smells that. He knows the team needs the quality starts. "He also sees the other starters doing really well, and I think internally that motivates him. And he's just been able to make a lot of really good pitches here lately." Buehler is 2-0 with a 4.00 ERA in three starts against the Rays. Cash will turn to steady Nick Martinez (13-4, 2.93) on Saturday. The All-Star will attempt to earn the win for the fourth time in his past five starts. In his most recent outing, the 36-year-old Miami native was brilliant against the Baltimore Orioles. He fired six innings of one-hit, shutout ball with four strikeouts. Martinez is 1-4 with a 4.88 ERA in five appearances (four starts) against the Padres. --Field Level Media

item.title: Royals remain optimistic ahead of rematch vs. Guardians
item.description: Bobby Witt Jr. hasn't given up on the Kansas City Royals' postseason dreams. Neither has manager Matt Quatraro. Until they officially are eliminated, it's still game on.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Bobby Witt Jr. hasn't given up on the Kansas City Royals' postseason dreams. Neither has manager Matt Quatraro. Until they officially are eliminated, it's still game on. Red-hot Kansas City continues its late-season push on Saturday afternoon, playing the middle contest in a three-game series at the Cleveland Guardians. Daniel Lynch IV (4-4, 2.93 ERA) will get the start for the Royals on Saturday opposite fellow left-hander Foster Griffin (15-4, 3.19) of the Guardians. Cleveland currently holds the third wild-card position in the American League by two games over the Texas Rangers and Baltimore Orioles, but Kansas City has moved within 7 1/2 of the Guardians with 26 games on its schedule. The Royals have won 11 of their last 12, including a 3-0 victory Friday in Cleveland that featured eight brilliant innings and a season-high 10 strikeouts from All-Star pitcher Michael Wacha. "We're just trying to enjoy each and every day, and have fun playing baseball together," Witt said amidst the disco-like scene in the clubhouse. "Things are going very well for us right now. We'll see where we are at the end of the season." Witt has led the charge by reaching base safely in 22 of 23 games since spending time on the injured list with lower back tightness. He scored the first run in the series opener after doubling high off the wall in left field off Tanner Bibee. Teammate Vinnie Pasquantino teased him for not clearing the fence, saying, "You've got no power." Witt immediately fired back with, "I have speed," pointing out Pasquantino's blunder on the basepaths in the fifth. Vibes undeniably are good around the team, which is why the lights were out and the music was loud as the players changed clothes. "This is a crazy game, so you just keep playing because you never know," Quatraro said. "We had a good win tonight. Every game with these guys (Cleveland) is tense, so getting one is big." Lynch has bounced between the rotation and bullpen since his last win on July 25, appearing in seven games with two losses and a 5.40 ERA in 15 innings. He has made 14 career appearances against Cleveland, six starts, and has a 1-4 record and 5.90 ERA. The 6-foot-6, 200-pounder, who has worked in 50 games this season, is thriving in the role with a career-low 2.93 ERA. The Guardians had won seven straight until being held to six hits by Wacha and closer Steven Cruz. That streak began immediately after they dropped to a season-low five games below .500 on Aug. 19. Rookie outfielder Chase DeLauter is hitting .347 with two homers and eight RBIs in 20 games this month, while catcher Patrick Bailey has a .467 average in his last six contests. "When you win seven straight, the first loss after feels a little bit bad because you just had gotten used to winning again," Cleveland second baseman Travis Bazzana said. "So it feels a little down, but we're ready to bounce back tomorrow. We feel like we're in a good spot to go win ballgames." Griffin ranks third in the majors in victories, one behind Sonny Gray of the Boston Red Sox and Cristopher Sanchez of the Philadelphia Phillies. Cleveland acquired him from the Washington Nationals on Aug. 3 in exchange for four prospects. The 31-year-old broke into the big leagues with Kansas City in 2020 but didn't pitch against them until this season. He gave up one run in six innings in a no-decision on June 16 in Washington. In four starts with the Guardians, Griffin is 3-1 with a 4.05 ERA. His last three outings have been wins, covering 16 total innings with a 2.25 ERA and 13 strikeouts. "We come to the field the same way every day, we do the little things right," Bibee said. "It's just like, 'We need to win today.' That's kind of the case every September." --Field Level Media

item.title: Nepal reanuda operaciones de rescate por aluvión y pide ayuda técnica y fondos millonarios
item.description: Nepal reanudó el sábado las labores de búsqueda y rescate tras una breve suspensión debida a las condiciones meteorológicas, mientras las autoridades busca a cerca de 3.000 personas desaparecidas tras una devastadora riada que se cobró la vida de cientos de personas y arrasó una región fronteriza con el Tíbet.
item.dc:creator: Gopal Sharma, Saurabh Sharma, Sahana Bajracharya, Liz Lee
item.content:encoded: Nepal reanudó el sábado las labores de búsqueda y rescate tras una breve suspensión debida a las condiciones meteorológicas, mientras las autoridades busca a cerca de 3.000 personas desaparecidas tras una devastadora riada que se cobró la vida de cientos de personas y arrasó una región fronteriza con el Tíbet. Esta empobrecida nación del Himalaya, con una población de 30 millones de personas, solicitó ayuda especializada del extranjero y su ministro de Hacienda declaró a Reuters que también necesitaría entre 4.000 y 5.000 millones de dólares para la reconstrucción tras la catástrofe. Provocado por el derrumbe de un glaciar, un torrente de rocas, hielo, barro y escombros arrasó el miércoles los sistemas fluviales de montaña, causando la muerte de al menos 669 personas en Nepal y siete en el Tíbet chino, y arrasando edificios, puentes y centrales eléctricas. Casi 3.000 personas siguen desaparecidas, incluidas unas 2.426 en Nepal y 554 en el condado de Gyirong, en el Tíbet, entre las que se encuentran al menos 540 ciudadanos extranjeros, muchos de ellos peregrinos hindúes procedentes de la India. CADÁVERES DESCOMPUESTOS Las operaciones de búsqueda y rescate se interrumpieron temporalmente debido a la lluvia y la niebla, pero se reanudaron a última hora de la tarde, según informó un agente de policía del distrito de Rasuwa, uno de los más afectados. "Los helicópteros están volando y la operación se ha reanudado tras una leve mejoría en las condiciones meteorológicas", afirmó, bajo condición de anonimato, ya que no está autorizado a hablar con los medios. Las autoridades también habían suspendido las labores de rescate el viernes, cuando un lago, formado en la frontera entre Nepal y China tras la inundación, comenzó a desbordarse hacia los ríos Lhende Khola y Trishuli de Nepal. El sábado, el riesgo había disminuido y ya se podían ver partes del lecho del lago, según informaron las autoridades chinas y la cadena estatal CCTV. Las imágenes por satélite sugerían que el agua se estaba drenando lentamente, reduciendo gradualmente su tamaño, informó la CCTV. El lago es uno de los dos situados aguas arriba de la zona inundada que Nepal mantiene bajo vigilancia. Los riesgos de inundación persistirán hasta que ambos se hayan vaciado por completo, advirtió un responsable. Tres días después de la catástrofe, las autoridades indicaron que algunos de los cadáveres recuperados se habían descompuesto hasta quedar irreconocibles. Serían enterrados tras cumplir con los trámites legales debido a los riesgos para la salud y al temor a brotes epidémicos. "Se tomarán muestras de ADN y los cadáveres serán enterrados en un espacio abierto", indicó la administración del distrito de Chitwan en un comunicado. LAS FAMILIAS BUSCAN A LOS DESAPARECIDOS En Katmandú, las familias de los desaparecidos se reunieron frente al Campus Médico de Maharajgunj, donde fueron trasladados algunos cadáveres. Muchos intentaron identificar a sus familiares a partir de las fotografías de los cadáveres expuestas en las puertas y muros perimetrales. En Malasia, las familias de 91 ciudadanos que figuraban como "ilocalizables" en el Tíbet y Nepal también esperaban noticias. Manivannan Rethinam, representante de algunos de ellos, instó al Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores a establecer un canal de comunicación para recibir información de forma más rápida, señalando que la falta de información resulta "profundamente dolorosa" para los familiares que esperaban noticias. El Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores de Malasia afirmó que continúan las labores de búsqueda, rescate y verificación. Para los supervivientes, la terrible experiencia está lejos de haber terminado, ya que se enfrentan a la tarea de reconstruir sus vidas. Saraswati Ghale, de 43 años, contó que su casa quedó destruida por la riada. Recordó haber subido a toda prisa la colina cuando llegó el agua, que sacudió el suelo "como si hubiera un terremoto". "No me queda nada (...) Me he salvado, pero quién sabe cómo acabarán las cosas", afirmó. El ministro de Hacienda de Nepal, Swarnim Wagle, declaró a Reuters que la estimación inicial del Gobierno es que la reconstrucción costará entre 4.000 y 5.000 millones de dólares. "Se trata solo de una estimación. Se están evaluando las pérdidas y los daños", añadió. LA AYUDA TÉCNICA SE DIRIGE A NEPAL El ministro de Relaciones Exteriores de Nepal, Shisir Khanal, pidió asistencia especializada para rescatar a las personas atrapadas en túneles, restablecer las vías de transporte y las líneas de comunicación en los lugares donde se habían destruido los puentes, identificar los cadáveres, realizar pruebas de ADN y conservar los cadáveres durante períodos más prolongados. "Ya hemos solicitado dichos servicios especializados y asistencia técnica en áreas en las que no contamos con la experiencia ni los conocimientos técnicos suficientes", comentó a Reuters a última hora del viernes. Un equipo de expertos indios en túneles llegó a Nepal el sábado, según indicó, mientras que la agencia de noticias china Xinhua informó de que Pekín había enviado a cinco expertos en túneles para apoyar las labores de rescate, a los que se unirán otros cuatro. India ya ha enviado tres vuelos con 60 toneladas de suministros de ayuda humanitaria, entre los que se incluyen mantas, medicamentos y alimentos. También ha ofrecido personal de respuesta ante catástrofes, puentes prefabricados y equipos técnicos para ayudar a restablecer las comunicaciones, según informó el Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores. Las autoridades chinas también intentan localizar a las más de 500 personas que siguen desaparecidas tras la inundación. Los equipos de rescate llegaron el viernes al complejo fronterizo de Gyirong, el más afectado, utilizando cuerdas para abrirse paso entre bosques y acantilados, ya que las carreteras están destruidas. En unas condiciones desoladoras y lluviosas el sábado por la mañana, más de 50 rescatistas peinaron los escombros de rocas y barro, buscando señales de vida y llamando a los supervivientes, según informó la CCTV.

item.title: Astros to toss patchwork of pitchers against Mets
item.description: The Houston Astros will have to cobble together their pitching plans for the final two games of their weekend series against the New York Mets.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Houston Astros will have to cobble together their pitching plans for the final two games of their weekend series against the New York Mets. Thanks to Hunter Brown and an assist from the Milwaukee Brewers, such a piecemeal problem is a lot less concerning than it might have been entering Friday. The Astros will look to continue their resurgence Saturday afternoon when they visit the Mets in the second contest of the three-game interleague set. Left-hander Bennett Sousa (1-3, 6.27 ERA) will serve as an opener for the Astros in his first big league start. Cristian Javier (1-4, 6.47 ERA) likely will follow in a bulk relief role. Right-hander Nolan McLean (9-8, 3.21) is slated to start for the Mets. Brown struck out a season-high 10 batters over 6 2/3 innings Friday night, when he earned the win as the Astros beat the Mets, 3-1. Brown's gem, coupled with the Milwaukee Brewers' 6-1 win over the Texas Rangers, increased Houston's American League West lead over the second-place Rangers to two games. The Astros will win any tiebreaker by virtue of a 9-4 edge in the season series with their Lone Star State rivals. The Astros are 3-1 since the exit of general manager Dana Brown on Monday. Houston, which is trying to return to the playoffs after its streak of nine straight postseason appearances was snapped last year, continued tinkering Thursday, when former pitching coach Brent Strom returned to the team as a consultant. Strom, pitching coach Joshua Miller and assistant pitching coach Ethan Katz will be tasked with figuring out a way to repair a rotation that has issued a league-high 330 walks while compiling a 5.11 ERA - third-worst in the majors - and averaging just 4.9 innings per outing. Neither Javier nor whomever starts Sunday's game - the Astros currently have "TBD" as their probable pitcher - likely are to approach the length provided Friday by Brown, who was the first Astros pitcher to pitch at least six innings since Hayden Wesneski lasted seven innings against the San Francisco Giants on Aug. 10. "That's huge, just to get him out there in the seventh and us being able to save some bullets for the next few days," Astros manager Joe Espada said. McLean has provided plenty of relief for the Mets' bullpen by lasting at least six innings in 12 of his last 14 starts. He's gone 6-4 with a 2.40 ERA in that span to drop his overall ERA from 4.21 to 3.21 - the lowest it has been since McLean had a 2.92 ERA following his start on May 14. McLean has gone at least six innings 17 times overall in 26 starts this season - more than twice as often as Sean Manaea, who ranks second on the Mets with eight outings of six innings or more. "I wouldn't say I am any stronger or any better than I felt to start the season," McLean said following his start against the Chicago White Sox last Sunday, when he tossed six scoreless innings of one-hit ball and didn't factor into the decision in the Mets' 2-1 loss. "It's just every time I go out there, I am trying to learn and hopefully doing a better job of that." Sousa took the defeat in his most recent outing Wednesday night, when he gave up four runs while recording just one out in the Astros' 9-3 loss to the Yankees. Javier last pitched Sunday, when he didn't factor into the decision after allowing three runs over four innings as the starter in a 7-6 loss to the Athletics. Sousa has never opposed the Mets. Javier didn't factor into the decision in his lone start against New York on June 21, 2023, when he surrendered four runs over 2 1/3 innings in the Astros' 10-8 victory. McLean has never faced the Astros. -Field Level Media

item.title: Braves seek sixth straight win, as they face woeful Rockies
item.description: The Atlanta Braves will continue their quest to avoid the wild-card round in October when they host the Colorado Rockies in the second game of their three-game series on Saturday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Atlanta Braves will continue their quest to avoid the wild-card round in October when they host the Colorado Rockies in the second game of their three-game series on Saturday night. The National League-East leaders defeated the Rockies 6-4 on Friday and enter the Saturday contest a game behind the Los Angeles Dodgers in the chase for the No. 2 seed in the league. The top two seeds earn byes straight into the NL Division Series. Atlanta helped its cause by sweeping the Dodgers in a trio of one-run games ahead of the series against the Rockies and extended its winning streak to five games with Friday's triumph. The Braves can make it two in a row against the Rockies when they send left-hander Martin Perez (8-8, 3.12 ERA) to the mound. Colorado will counter with right-hander Ryan Feltner (5-8, 6.08) Perez is slated to make his ninth career start against Colorado and is 2-3 with a 3.60 ERA in his eight previous outings. He is following two strong starts by Chris Sale and Grant Holmes in wins over the Dodgers and Rockies, respectively. It also comes after the team announced two of its starters, Spencer Schwellenbach and Hurston Waldrep, are done for the season and will undergo elbow surgery. The Braves have been winning despite Ronald Acuna Jr.'s struggles in August. A career .284 hitter, he is batting .235 on the season and .227 in August. Manager Walt Weiss gave him Thursday off. Acuna responded with three hits and a walk, and he also made a sliding catch in right field. "I've talked about this, picking spots for guys when I think I feel like maybe they can use some help slowing things down," Weiss said Thursday. "We talk about the fact that I think with everyday players, the best way to slow the game down, or one of the best ways, is to have them watch it in the dugout." Colorado's Hunter Goodman returned Tuesday from a left shoulder strain that cost him 10 games. He made an impact right away, homering in each of his first two games back against the host Nationals to give him a career-high 36 homers. He added three hits Friday night. The two-time All-Star catcher continues to impress manager Warren Schaeffer. "He's awesome," Schaeffer said. "He's our All-Star. He's got 30-plus homers. It's always great to get a guy like that back in the lineup. He feels good, which is even better." Even with Goodman's strong season, the Rockies are on pace to lose 100 games again, although they already surpassed last season's 43 wins with more than a month remaining in the season. Still, at 52-83, Colorado has the worst record in the NL. One of the disappointments is Feltner's recent outings. He had a serviceable June, posting a 4.00 ERA in five starts, but followed that with a 9.68 ERA in July and a 7.00 ERA in four August starts. He is 3-6 in the nine starts. His past two starts have been especially tough. He allowed seven runs in a 7-6 loss to the Dodgers on Aug. 18, then gave up seven runs (five earned) to the Nationals on Monday. He is facing Atlanta for the fifth time in his career, and is 0-4 with an 11.25 ERA in his previous four starts. He has given up six home runs in 16 innings. --Field Level Media

item.title: Cardinals follow innings limit as Kyle Leahy faces Pirates
item.description: Right-hander Kyle Leahy has been a bright spot for the St. Louis Cardinals this season, but to protect his promising future, the team is limiting his innings the rest of the way.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Right-hander Kyle Leahy has been a bright spot for the St. Louis Cardinals this season, but to protect his promising future, the team is limiting his innings the rest of the way. Leahy (10-4, 3.13 ERA) makes his 26th start Saturday afternoon, facing the visiting Pittsburgh Pirates in the second contest of a three-game set. The Cards opened the series with a 4-1 victory Friday night. A big key was the performance of rookie left-hander Quinn Mathews, who allowed a run and struck out seven over 5 2/3 innings for his first major league win. With Mathews pitching into the sixth, and right-hander Ryan Fernandez following with two scoreless innings, the rest of the pitching staff got a much-needed break. And it was important with Leahy starting the next game. "That's exactly what's needed," Cardinals manager Oliver Marmol said. "Knowing that you have a shorter start with our guy Leahy tomorrow, Quinn being able to do what he did today was very important." Leahy's 126 1/3 innings are his most since posting 144 2/3 in 2022 between Double-A Springfield and Triple-A Memphis. Leahy, 29, had been a reliever for the Cardinals in his first two full major league seasons. Leahy pitched at least six innings on six occasions this season, including three straight starts in July. He's been scaling back in August and threw just four scoreless, two-hit innings in his previous start Sunday in a 6-4 loss to the Philadelphia Phillies. The Cardinals are 4 1/2 games behind the final spot in the NL wild-card race, trailing the San Diego Padres, Arizona Diamondbacks, and Miami Marlins. But having Leahy healthy going into next season weighs heavily, even with the Cardinals still on the fringe of postseason contention in 2026. Against the Pirates, he's posted a 1.93 ERA with 22 strikeouts in 14 innings the past two seasons combined. He got the win in an 11-7 victory in a start that lasted 5 1/3 innings at Pittsburgh on April 28. Pirates slugger Oneil Cruz homered that day. The Pirates have faded from postseason contention and now just want to return to the higher-quality play they showed during the first few months of the season. They've had trouble scoring runs on their current road trip, and they made three errors in the field against the Cardinals in the series opener. Pirates manager Don Kelly said his team wants to reset after an inconsistent stretch on both sides of the ball. "We need to get back to doing what we do, which we've talked a lot about -- keeping the line moving, finding a way to have team at-bats, and trusting each other going through the process," Kelly said. "We're getting outside of that right now. Guys going up there trying to carry it, and it's not on any one player personally." Lake Bachar (1-3, 3.70) will start as an opener for the Pirates, with fellow right-hander Carmen Mlodzinski (6-6, 4.17) expected to follow as a bulk reliever. In 11 career appearances (four starts) Mlodzinski is 3-0 with a 1.75 ERA. --Field Level Media

item.content:encoded: Europa está haciendo declaraciones que sugieren que considera a Rusia como un "adversario e, incluso, un enemigo", afirmó el sábado el portavoz del Kremlin, Dmitri Peskov, quien añadió que Moscú no ve perspectivas de mejora en las relaciones entre Rusia y la Unión Europea.
